import pandas as pd

source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_78/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_78/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source0 and Source1 on Prod_id
df = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="Prod_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source2 on Cust_id
df = pd.merge(df, source2, on="Cust_id", how="inner")

# The target examples have 4199 rows, the join results in 4200 rows (one extra)
# The target examples have no primary key or unique key constraints given,
# but the target examples show no duplicates, so we apply a groupby on all columns to remove duplicates if any.

# Group by all columns to remove duplicates (no aggregation needed)
group_by_cols = ['Ord_id', 'Prod_id', 'Ship_id', 'Cust_id', 'Sales', 'Discount', 'Order_Quantity', 'Profit',

                 'Customer_Name', 'Province', 'Region', 'Customer_Segment']

df = df.groupby(group_by_cols, as_index=False).size()  # size() just to trigger groupby, but we don't need the count
df = df[group_by_cols]  # keep only the grouped columns (dropping the size column)

# Write the final output
